sentence_stem: I wanted to go to the park, but
full_sentence: I wanted to go to the park, but it was raining.

options.text: I went to the park with my friend.
options.why_wrong: This continues the same idea without any contrast. 'But' needs a clause that shows the opposite of what the speaker wanted.

options.text: so I went to the park.
options.why_wrong: 'So' shows a result, not a contrast. Use 'but' here to show that something stopped the plan.
'And' adds more information but does not show contrast. This clause does not explain why the plan did not happen.

explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast with the wish in the first part of the sentence, so we need a clause that gives the obstacle. Ukrainian speakers sometimes choose a simple result link here because their first language often uses one connector for both cause and contrast.
translation: Я хотів піти в парк, але йшов дощ.
